questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.learningObjective: Differentiate implicitly to find dy/dx
questions.stem: First differentiate x^2+y^2=1 implicitly, then solve for y'.

options.misconception: sign error — treating "2x+2y y'=0 -> y'=y/x" as the answer

questions.explanation: "2x+2y y'=0 -> y'=-x/y" is correct. The rule behind it: Treat y as function. This is the skill the item tests: Differentiate implicitly to find dy/dx. The alternatives are tempting for identifiable reasons — "2x+2y y'=0 -> y'=y/x" (sign error — treating "2x+2y y'=0 -> y'=y/x" as the answer); "2x+2y=0 -> y'=-x/y" (forgets y' on y term); "2x+2y y'=1 -> y'=(1-2x)/(2y)" (differentiates constant as 1). Each of those errors misses what implicit differentiation requires, so the keyed option stands.
